A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same frozen visual Unicode embedding research. All eight pages of v1 and nineteen pages of v4 are readable, including figures, tables, and v4's Appendices A and B. v1 has no appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original tokenizer comparisons, model training curves, benchmark scores, and embedding visualizations in Figures 1–7.

after.justification: v4 reports original training and benchmark results, initialization ablations, internal-layer visualizations, and numerical training trajectories in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The proposed glyph-rendering, resizing, PCA, normalization, and freezing pipeline remains unchanged. The expanded tokenizer description documents the existing vocabulary family; the new index and random embeddings serve as experimental controls rather than replacing the proposed visual method.

E1.justification: v1 Figure 5 includes SQuAD evaluation results, which disappear from v4's reported evaluations, although SQuAD-v2 remains training data. The principal Wikipedia languages, multilingual tokenizer coverage, MMLU, ARC, and CommonsenseQA remain represented.

E2.justification: Beyond the retained trainable-embedding baseline, v4 evaluates sequential 16-bit identifiers and random 64-, 256-, and 1024-dimensional embeddings, each with corresponding PCA/normalization variants. Figure 4 also adds SmolLM and SmolLM2 at 135M and 360M parameters. These substantially expand the comparator set; the GPT-2 score mentioned in prose is contextual rather than a newly reported controlled comparison.

E3.justification: The reported setup changes from 0.2B/0.4B/0.5B models with 65,536- or 131,072-token vocabularies to approximately 0.3B models with 65,536 tokens. The stated training corpus changes from approximately 9B to 4B tokens, and maximum batch size changes from 16 to 18. The new representation analysis also introduces a 70-word, seven-category activation-probing protocol.

E4.justification: v1 visualizes input embeddings but lacks nonvisual frozen controls. v4 adds ablations testing visual information, embedding dimensionality, and PCA/normalization through sequential-index and random embeddings (Sections 3.1 and 5.4). Figures 8–11 additionally examine the authors' trained models across input embeddings, attention projections, and early and late Transformer blocks.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. v4's additional initialization variants and training trajectories do not constitute uncertainty estimation across replicated runs.

E6.justification: v1 reports MMLU scores of 22.29 for best_bvv_ru and 11.37 for its trainable counterpart; v4 reports 23.81 for Model_UNI_GLIF and 12.54 for Model_unfrozen under different model and data settings, so these are replacement results rather than same-setting gains. v4 adds comparator and ablation scores, internal-layer findings, and Appendix B's numerical loss/perplexity trajectories, while removing the earlier size/language-specific results and SQuAD score row.

T1.justification: Neither version presents formal theorems, proofs, or a developed mathematical theory. The retained embedding construction is mathematically unchanged; the new interference explanations and representation analyses are qualitative arguments and empirical investigations.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion are unchanged, and the introduction retains the same contribution list: semantic emergence without trainable input embeddings, universal visual embeddings, representational interference, and released implementations. New controls and visualizations support these existing claims rather than redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: v4 extends the original orthographic-versus-semantic interference explanation into a conflict between token discrimination and semantic proximity, including gradient imprinting and the sufficiency of arbitrary fixed identifiers. It also explains the existing visual clusters through pixel density and PCA, and contextualizes the SmolLM comparison through differing training-data volumes. The explicit scale and modality limitations in Section 6.3 remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 substantially expands implementation disclosure: n-gram extraction and Unicode allocation, layer/head counts, rotary embeddings, untied output weights, parameter breakdowns, and the repetition mapping for 16-dimensional controls. It also specifies training/validation token counts, gradient accumulation, evaluation intervals, and final-checkpoint selection. These details improve reproducibility without themselves establishing changes to previously unspecified settings; repository and model access links remain the same.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds previously absent, directly relevant glyph/pixel research by Salesky et al., Wang et al., Dai and Cai, and Liu et al. It explicitly positions the work against trainable or auxiliary visual features used for downstream tasks, substantially expanding discussion of the closest prior research. SmolLM/SmolLM2 references are added, while the ERNIE and ALBERT bibliography entries are removed.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. Editorial changes include organizing tokenizer construction into three subsections, expanding selected explanations, removing a repetitive discussion paragraph, and adding headings for the new analyses and appendices. The revision is not a wholesale rewrite of the existing narrative.

P2.justification: v4 replaces the two-column presentation with a single-column layout and substantially redesigns the experimental displays: combined model curves, revised benchmark heatmaps, and new multi-panel activation and ablation figures. The unchanged input-embedding plots are enlarged and relocated. The model inventory moves to Appendix A with revised rows and columns, and Appendix B adds a numerical training table.

improvement.justification: v4 addresses an important weakness of v1 by adding nonvisual frozen controls that help distinguish visual information from freezing and identifier sufficiency. Internal-layer probes examine semantic emergence beyond the input-only visualizations, while substantially fuller implementation details make the experiments easier to assess and reproduce. The narrower model-size and evaluation coverage is a tradeoff, and uncertainty reporting and causal validation of interference remain absent. Nevertheless, the better experimental controls and transparency provide a substantial net improvement.
